reforms.description: The Canadian government presented its Innovation Strategy in 2002, aiming to encourage innovation and improve skills across the country, with specific targets for R&D performance and community innovation. The March 2004 federal budget included additional spending to support the commercialization of research, emphasizing funding for CIHR, NSERC, SSHRC, universities, and research hospitals, alongside an allocation of C$60 million to strengthen Genome Canada's research capabilities.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The reforms aim to enhance R&D performance and support commercialization, which are expected to boost innovation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The reforms were explicitly stated as implemented in the 2004 federal budget.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reforms involve significant funding increases and strategic initiatives but do not represent a complete overhaul of the system.
reforms.source_quote: Additional spending through a range of channels (including CIHR, NSERC, SSHRC, universities and research hospitals, and Genome Canada) with special emphasis on support for commercialisation of research.

reforms.description: The Canadian government announced further funding for R&D in specific areas in the 2004 Budget, alongside the establishment of a private sector-led group to reduce administrative burdens on small and medium-sized enterprises.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The funding aims to enhance R&D capabilities, which is expected to foster innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The funding was part of the 2004 Budget, which was implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The funding is significant but does not represent a major structural change.
reforms.source_quote: Further funding for R&D in specific areas was announced in the 2004 Budget, along with a new private sector-led group to focus on reducing administrative burdens on small and medium-sized enterprises.

reforms.description: The March 2004 federal budget increased the capital cost allowance rates for computer and broadband equipment, aiming to stimulate investment in technology and infrastructure.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The increase in capital cost allowance rates is designed to encourage investment in technology, which can enhance productivity and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The reform was part of the 2004 federal budget, which was implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform is a minor adjustment to existing tax incentives rather than a major overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: Increase in the capital cost allowance (i.e. depreciation) rate for computer equipment from 30 per cent to 45 per cent and in the rate for broadband, Internet and other data network infrastructure equipment from 20 per cent to 30 per cent.

reforms.description: The Canadian government provided an annual increase of C$90 million to the three federal granting councils that fund basic research, along with additional funding to offset indirect costs of research and support Genome Canada.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increasing funding for basic research is expected to enhance knowledge creation and innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: The funding increase was explicitly stated as implemented in the 2004 federal budget.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant increase in funding for basic research, which is a structural change in support for R&D.
reforms.source_quote: Funding provided in the 2004 federal budget: annual increase of C$90 million to Canada’s three federal granting councils which fund basic research.

reforms.description: Enhancements to the application process for the Scientific Research and Experimental Development tax credit were implemented to improve accessibility for universities and research hospitals.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improving accessibility to tax credits is expected to encourage more R&D investment by universities and research hospitals.
reforms.status_evidence: The enhancements were explicitly stated as implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform is an administrative adjustment rather than a major policy change.
reforms.source_quote: Since 2002, a number of service enhancements have been implemented to improve the application process for the Scientific Research and Experimental Development tax credit.

reforms.description: The First Ministers agreed on a 10-year action plan on health, which includes new funding to improve access to care and reduce wait times for essential medical services.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The action plan aims to enhance healthcare access and efficiency, which can lead to better health outcomes and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The action plan was agreed upon but not yet implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: This reform represents a significant commitment to improving health services and funding over a decade.
reforms.source_quote: On 13-15 September 2004 the First Ministers met in Ottawa and agreed on a 10-year action plan on health with a view to improving access to care and reducing wait times.
